items.informal_name: Univariate Embedding Equals Rename Composition in Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {σ : Type u_3} [inst : CommSemiring R] (i : σ),
  Polynomial.toMvPolynomial i = (MvPolynomial.rename fun x => i).comp ↑(MvPolynomial.pUnitAlgEquiv R).symm
items.informal_description: The algebra homomorphism embedding a univariate polynomial ring $ R[X] $ into the multivariate polynomial ring $ R[\sigma] $ by substituting $ X $ with the $ i $-th variable in $ \sigma $ is equal to the composition of the inverse of the algebra equivalence between $ R[\mathsf{PUnit}] $ and $ R[X] $ with the renaming of variables from $ \mathsf{PUnit} $ to the $ i $-th variable in $ \sigma $.

items.informal_name: Compatibility of Variable Renaming with Polynomial Evaluation in Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ (R : Type u) [inst : CommSemiring R] {σ : Type u_2} {τ : Type u_3} (f : σ → τ) (i : σ) (p : Polynomial R),
  (MvPolynomial.rename f) ((Polynomial.aeval (MvPolynomial.X i)) p) = (Polynomial.aeval (MvPolynomial.X (f i))) p
items.informal_description: For any function $ f : \sigma \to \tau $, variable $ i \in \sigma $, and polynomial $ p \in R[X] $, renaming the variables in the evaluation of $ p $ at $ X_i $ via $ f $ yields the same result as evaluating $ p $ at the renamed variable $ X_{f(i)} $ in $ R[\tau] $. Formally, $ \text{rename} \, f \, (\text{aeval}(X_i, p)) = \text{aeval}(X_{f(i)}, p) $.

items.informal_name: Evaluation Equivalence for Multivariate Polynomials over Unit Type
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_2} {S : Type u_3} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : CommSemiring S] {f : MvPolynomial PUnit.{u_4 + 1} R}
  {φ : R →+* S} {a : S}, Polynomial.eval₂ φ a ((MvPolynomial.pUnitAlgEquiv R) f) = MvPolynomial.eval₂ φ (fun x => a) f
items.informal_description: For any multivariate polynomial $ f $ over the unit type $ \mathsf{PUnit} $, ring homomorphism $ \varphi : R \to S $, and element $ a \in S $, evaluating the univariate polynomial obtained from $ f $ via the algebra equivalence $ \mathsf{pUnitAlgEquiv} $ at $ a $ using $ \varphi $ coincides with evaluating $ f $ directly with $ \varphi $ and the constant variable map sending the single variable to $ a $. This establishes that the two evaluation procedures yield identical results under the canonical isomorphism between multivariate polynomials over $ \mathsf{PUnit} $ and univariate polynomials.

items.informal_name: Evaluation Commutes with pUnit Algebra Equivalence Inverse
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_2} {S : Type u_3} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : CommSemiring S] {f : Polynomial R} {φ : R →+* S}
  {a : Unit → S}, MvPolynomial.eval₂ φ a ((MvPolynomial.pUnitAlgEquiv R).symm f) = Polynomial.eval₂ φ (a ()) f
items.informal_description: For any univariate polynomial $ f \in R[X] $, ring homomorphism $ \varphi : R \to S $, and element $ a \in S $, evaluating the multivariate polynomial $ (\mathsf{pUnit}\text{-}\mathsf{AlgEquiv}^{-1}(f)) $ at $ \varphi $ and the constant function $ \mathsf{Unit} \to S $ mapping $ () \mapsto a $ yields the same result as evaluating $ f $ at $ \varphi $ and $ a $. Formally, $ \mathsf{eval}_2(\varphi, a)(\mathsf{pUnit}\text{-}\mathsf{AlgEquiv}^{-1}(f)) = f.\mathsf{eval}_2(\varphi, a) $.

items.informal_name: Compatibility of Evaluation with Algebra Equivalence for Multivariate Polynomials over Unit Type
items.informal_description: For any multivariate polynomial $ f $ in $ R[\mathsf{PUnit}] $, ring homomorphism $ \varphi : R \to S $, and evaluation map $ a : \mathsf{PUnit} \to S $, evaluating the univariate polynomial obtained via the algebra equivalence $ \mathsf{PUnitAlgEquiv} $ at $ \varphi $ and $ a(\mathsf{default}) $ equals evaluating $ f $ directly using $ \varphi $ and $ a $. Symbolically: $ (\mathsf{PUnitAlgEquiv}(f)).\mathsf{eval}_2(\varphi, a(\ast)) = f.\mathsf{eval}_2(\varphi, a) $, where $ \ast $ denotes the unique element of $ \mathsf{PUnit} $.

items.type: (R : Type u) → [inst : CommSemiring R] → MvPolynomial PUnit.{u_2 + 1} R ≃ₐ[R] Polynomial R
items.informal_description: The algebra equivalence between the multivariate polynomial ring $ R[\mathsf{PUnit}] $ (where $ \mathsf{PUnit} $ is the unit type with one element) and the univariate polynomial ring $ R[X] $. This equivalence is constructed by evaluating multivariate polynomials via the constant polynomial embedding $ \mathsf{C} $ and indeterminate mapping $ X $, with the inverse given by evaluating univariate polynomials back into the multivariate ring using $ \mathsf{C} $ and the unit-type variable. The equivalence preserves addition, multiplication, and scalar multiplication by elements of $ R $, establishing an isomorphism of $ R $-algebras.

That is, the canonical map $\mathbb{Z}[\alpha] \to \mathbb{Z}[\beta]$ constructed via the free functor coincides with the polynomial ring homomorphism that renames variables according to $f$.

items.informal_name: Univariate Embedding Equals Rename Composition in Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {σ : Type u_3} [inst : CommSemiring R] (i : σ),
  Polynomial.toMvPolynomial i = (MvPolynomial.rename fun x => i).comp ↑(MvPolynomial.pUnitAlgEquiv R).symm
items.informal_description: The algebra homomorphism embedding a univariate polynomial ring $ R[X] $ into the multivariate polynomial ring $ R[\sigma] $ by substituting $ X $ with the $ i $-th variable in $ \sigma $ is equal to the composition of the inverse of the algebra equivalence between $ R[\mathsf{PUnit}] $ and $ R[X] $ with the renaming of variables from $ \mathsf{PUnit} $ to the $ i $-th variable in $ \sigma $.

items.informal_name: Compatibility of Variable Renaming with Univariate Polynomial Embedding
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {σ : Type u_3} {τ : Type u_4} [inst : CommSemiring R] (f : σ → τ) (a : σ),
  (MvPolynomial.rename f).comp (Polynomial.toMvPolynomial a) = Polynomial.toMvPolynomial (f a)
items.informal_description: For any function $ f : \sigma \to \tau $ and any $ a \in \sigma $, the composition of the multivariate polynomial variable renaming homomorphism induced by $ f $ and the univariate polynomial embedding at $ a $ equals the univariate polynomial embedding at $ f(a) $. Formally, $ \text{rename}_f \circ \text{toMvPolynomial}_a = \text{toMvPolynomial}_{f(a)} $ as $ R $-algebra homomorphisms.

items.informal_name: Compatibility of Variable Renaming with Univariate Polynomial Embedding
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {σ : Type u_3} {τ : Type u_4} [inst : CommSemiring R] (f : σ → τ) (a : σ) (p : Polynomial R),
  (MvPolynomial.rename f) ((Polynomial.toMvPolynomial a) p) = (Polynomial.toMvPolynomial (f a)) p
items.informal_description: For any function $ f : \sigma \to \tau $, element $ a \in \sigma $, and polynomial $ p \in R[X] $, renaming variables in the multivariate polynomial obtained by substituting $ X $ with $ a $ in $ p $ according to $ f $ yields the same result as substituting $ X $ with $ f(a) $ in $ p $ and then converting to a multivariate polynomial. Formally, $ \text{rename}(f)(p.\text{toMvPolynomial}(a)) = p.\text{toMvPolynomial}(f(a)) $.

items.informal_name: Algebra Homomorphism from Composed Generators with Renaming Equals Constant Embedding
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {S : Type v} {ι : Type w} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : CommRing S] [inst_2 : Algebra R S]
  {ι' : Type u_3} {T : Type u_7} [inst_3 : CommRing T] [inst_4 : Algebra R T] [inst_5 : Algebra S T]
  [inst_6 : IsScalarTower R S T] (Q : Algebra.Generators S T ι') (P : Algebra.Generators R S ι) (p : P.Ring),
  (Q.ofComp P).toAlgHom ((MvPolynomial.rename Sum.inr) p) = MvPolynomial.C ((algebraMap P.Ring S) p)
items.informal_description: For algebras $ R 	o S 	o T $ with generator structures $ P $ and $ Q $, composing $ Q $ with $ P $ and renaming variables via $ \text{Sum.inr} $ induces an $ R $-algebra homomorphism that evaluates a polynomial $ p \in P.\text{Ring} $ as the constant polynomial $ C(\text{algebraMap}(p)) $ in $ Q.\text{Ring} $.

items.informal_name: Algebra equivalence between multivariate polynomials over Fin(n+1) and polynomials in one variable with coefficients in multivariate polynomials over Fin(n)
items.type:
(R : Type u) →
  [inst : CommSemiring R] → (n : ℕ) → MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) R ≃ₐ[R] Polynomial (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R)
items.informal_description: The algebra equivalence between the ring of multivariate polynomials with variables indexed by $\text{Fin}(n+1)$ and coefficients in a commutative semiring $R$, and the polynomial ring in one variable whose coefficients are multivariate polynomials over $R$ with variables indexed by $\text{Fin}(n)$. This equivalence is constructed by renaming variables via the bijection $\text{Fin}(n+1) \simeq \text{Option}(\text{Fin}(n))$, mapping the $\text{none}$ case to the outer polynomial indeterminate and $\text{some } k$ cases to inner variables, with the inverse given by substituting renamed variables. The operation preserves addition, multiplication, and scalar multiplication by elements of $R$.

items.type: {R : Type u_1} {σ : Type u_3} {τ : Type u_4} [CommSemiring R] (f : σ → τ) (a : σ) : (MvPolynomial.rename f).comp (Polynomial.toMvPolynomial a) = Polynomial.toMvPolynomial (f a)

items.name: Polynomial.toMvPolynomial_eq_rename_comp
items.type: {R : Type u_1} {σ : Type u_3} [CommSemiring R] (i : σ) : Polynomial.toMvPolynomial i = (MvPolynomial.rename fun x => i).comp ↑(MvPolynomial.uniqueAlgEquiv R Unit).symm
